'''Fred Alan Wolf''' (born December 3, 1934) is an American theoretical physicist specializing in [[quantum physics]] and the relationship between physics and [[consciousness]]. He is a former physics professor at San Diego State University, and has helped to popularize science on the [[Discovery Channel]]. He is the author of a number of physics-themed books including ''Taking the Quantum Leap'' (1981), ''The Dreaming Universe'' (1994), ''Mind into Matter'' (2000), and ''Time Loops and Space Twists'' (2011).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/rn/newdimensions/stories/1999/59258.htm |title=Australian Broadcasting Corporation biographical sketch |access-date=2007-02-27 |publisher=ABC Online |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114174147/http://www.abc.net.au/rn/newdimensions/stories/1999/59258.htm |archive-date=November 14, 2007 }}</ref>

Wolf was a member in the 1970s, with [[Jack Sarfatti]] and others, of the [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]]'s [[Fundamental Fysiks Group]] founded in May 1975 by [[Elizabeth Rauscher]] and George Weissmann.<ref>Kaiser, David. [http://forum-network.org/lecture/how-hippies-saved-physics "Lecture: How the Hippies Saved Physics"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716205057/http://forum-network.org/lecture/how-hippies-saved-physics |date=2011-07-16 }}, WGBH PBS, April 28, 2010, from time index 0:04:00, and particularly from time index 0:11:00 and 0:23:00.
*[[David Kaiser (physicist)|Kaiser, David]]. ''How the Hippies Saved Physics: Science, Counterculture, and the Quantum Revival''. W. W. Norton & Co Inc., 2011.</ref> His theories about the interrelation of consciousness and quantum physics were described by ''Newsweek'' in 2007 as "on the fringes of mainstream science."<ref>[http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/newsweek-no-new-thinking-in-rhonda-byrnes-publishing-phenom-the-secret-just-new-marketing-newsweek-concludes-58073047.html "No New Thinking in Rhonda Byrne's Publishing Phenom 'The Secret'"], ''Newsweek'', February 25, 2007.</ref>

==Biography==
Born into a [[Jewish]] family,<ref>David Ian Miller, ''[https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/FINDING-MY-RELIGION-Fred-Alan-Wolf-from-What-3176730.php FINDING MY RELIGION / Fred Alan Wolf from "What the Bleep Do We Know?" on spirituality]'', [[SFGate]], 4 April 2005</ref> Wolf's interest in physics began as a child when he viewed a newsreel depicting the world's [[Trinity test|first atomic explosion]]. Wolf received his Ph.D. in [[theoretical physics]] from [[UCLA]] in 1963 and began researching the field of high atmospheric particle behavior following a [[nuclear explosion]].<ref name=faw>{{cite web|url=http://www.fredalanwolf.com/#AK|title=Welcome to the Parallel Universes of Dr. Fred Alan Wolf AKA Dr. Quantum|last=Wolf|first=Fred Alan}}</ref>
He has appeared as the resident physicist on the Discovery Channel's ''The Know Zone'', was a participant in the [[PBS]] series ''[[Closer to Truth]]'',<ref>[http://cttdev.gps.caltech.edu/participants/fwolf Dr. Fred Alan Wolf] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070213070759/http://cttdev.gps.caltech.edu/participants/fwolf/ |date=2007-02-13 }}, participant in [[Closer to Truth]]</ref> and has appeared on radio talk shows and television shows across the United States and abroad.<ref name=faw /> He also appeared in the films ''[[What the Bleep Do We Know!?]]'' (2004),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.whatthebleep.com/|title=''What the Bleep?'' website|access-date=2006-05-08|archive-date=2007-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070511231341/http://www.whatthebleep.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''[[The Secret (2006 film)|The Secret]]'' (2006) and Spirit Space (2008).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spiritspacemovie.com/|title=''Spirit Space'' website|access-date=2008-04-09|archive-date=2009-04-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090428231032/http://spiritspacemovie.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has lectured on subjects related to quantum physics and consciousness since the 1960s, often under the name Dr. Quantum or Captain Quantum.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.whatthebleep.com/reviews/fred-wolf-june-05.shtml |title=What the Bleep do We Know!?™ & What the Bleep!? - Down the Rabbit Hole |access-date=2007-06-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930184429/http://www.whatthebleep.com/reviews/fred-wolf-june-05.shtml |archive-date=2007-09-30 }}</ref>  He is also featured in the documentary about the [[Dalai Lama]], titled ''[[Dalai Lama Renaissance]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dalailamafilm.com/|title=''Dalai Lama Renaissance Documentary Film'' website}}</ref>

His book ''Taking the Quantum Leap: The New Physics for Nonscientists'' won a 1982 U.S. [[National Book Award]] [[List of winners of the National Book Award#Science|in Science]].<ref name=nba1982>
[https://www.nationalbook.org/awards-prizes/national-book-awards-1982 "National Book Awards – 1982"]. [[National Book Foundation]]. Retrieved 2012-03-07.</ref><ref group=lower-alpha>This was the 1982 [[List of winners of the National Book Award#Science|award for paperback Science]]. From 1980 to 1983 in [[National Book Awards#History|National Book Awards history]] there were dual hardcover and paperback awards in most categories, and [[National Book Award for Nonfiction#nonfiction categories|multiple nonfiction subcategories]]. Most of the paperback award-winners were reprints of books eligible for previous awards; this one was original.</ref>

He has taught at [[San Diego State University]], the [[University of Paris]], the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], the [[University of London]], [[University of Paris at Orsay]] and [[Birkbeck, University of London|Birkbeck College]], London.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fredalanwolf.com/#AK|title=Fred Alan Wolf, Ph.D.}}</ref>
